title: Economic Fury Targets Iranian Missile and UAV Procurement Networks
summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's OFAC announced a new round of sanctions (April 21, 2026) targeting 14 individuals, entities, and aircraft in Iran, Türkiye, and the UAE as part of the 'Economic Fury' campaign, focusing on procurement networks for ballistic missiles, Shahed-series UAVs, and associated components. Secretary Bessent stated Treasury will continue to target the Iranian regime and those enabling its destabilizing activities, with this being the fifth round of nonproliferation designations tied to the September 2025 UN sanctions reimposition.
key_points: OFAC designated 14 individuals, entities, and aircraft for involvement in procuring or transporting weapons or weapons components on behalf of the Iranian regime
Targets include Pishgam Electronic Safeh Company (PESC) and associates for procuring thousands of servomotors with one-way attack UAV applications found in Shahed-136 UAVs
OFAC acted against Emti Fiber Textile (Türkiye-based) for shipping hundreds of shipments of cotton linters used to produce nitrocellulose for solid propellant rocket motors
Sanctions target ballistic missile propellant precursors including sodium perchlorate procured through companies Adak Pargas Pars and Pardisan Rezvan Shargh
Actions build on NSPM 2 directives to curtail Iran's ballistic missile program, counter weapons capabilities, deny Iran a nuclear weapon, and deny IRGC access to assets
Fifth round of nonproliferation designations in support of September 27, 2025 reimposition of UN sanctions following Iran's 'significant non-performance' of nuclear commitments
Actions taken pursuant to E.O. 13382 (WMD proliferators) and E.O. 13224 (terrorism)
why_it_matters: These sanctions represent escalation in the U.S. 'Economic Fury' campaign against Iran, directly targeting the supply chains for ballistic missiles and attack drones. Secretary Bessent explicitly cited threats to global energy markets and Iranian 'extortion of global energy markets,' making this relevant for energy sector risk assessment. The timing follows Iran's nuclear non-performance triggering UN sanctions reimposition in September 2025, signaling sustained pressure on Tehran's weapons programs. Energy commodities (crude oil) could face supply disruption risk from regional conflict escalation involving Iranian drones targeting regional energy infrastructure.
macro_context: The sanctions target Iran's ability to reconstitute ballistic missile inventories and produce Shahed-series UAVs for targeting energy infrastructure in the region. Secretary Bessent's explicit reference to Iranian 'extortion of global energy markets' signals that energy commodities (particularly crude oil) face potential supply disruption risk from regional conflict involving Iranian drones. This represents a geopolitical macro catalyst with implications for commodity prices and associated currencies.
